decision: Build a proprietary 3D standard rather than design to an emerging published API
state_before: no product, no revenue, three founders and a $0.50 preferred round
information_available: that no 3D industry standard yet existed; that its own technology could become one; the founders' prior work on single-chip graphics accelerators at Sun
unknowns: who decided, what was weighed, what was rejected - nothing in any held document
alternatives: NONE PRINTED in any held in-window document
constraints: a founding round priced at $0.50 per share and whatever the founders themselves contributed, which is not stated anywhere held
rationale: the company's own later framing only: developed in the absence of industry standards with the goal of establishing the Company's proprietary NV technology as a 3D graphics standard
expected_result: a proprietary standard adopted as the market's
actual_result: The NV1 was introduced in May 1995 and its sales stopped in the first quarter of 1996; the company ceased NV2 development and re-architected to Direct3D - all stated by the registrant in 1998

decision: Abandon the console-targeted line and re-architect to Microsoft's Direct3D for the mainstream PC
state_before: NV1 sales collapsing; NV2 in development; a $3,912K calendar year about to end
information_available: that the PC industry had by the end of 1996 broadly adopted Direct3D and OpenGL, per the company's own sentence
unknowns: the decision date, the internal debate, the cost already sunk in the cancelled NV2, whether any alternative platform was considered
alternatives: whether staying on the proprietary path was ever costed; no alternative is printed
constraints: cash used in operations of $6.1M in 1995 and $300K in 1996; total assets of $5,525K at 1996-12-31; a $2,500K development advance still on the balance sheet
rationale: the market had chosen APIs and the company had no other product line
expected_result: a single-chip 3D and 2D part competitive on price that OEMs would design in
actual_result: RIVA128 introduced August 1997; first revenue of the current line in Q3 1997; product revenue $5.2M then $22.1M in Q3 and Q4 1997 - inside the stage, not (PB)

decision: Raise the Series D at $5.26 per share, below the 1995 Series C price of $6.67
state_before: loss-making on every full period; two customers at 94% of 1997 revenue; the new product shipping weeks earlier
information_available: its own cash position and burn as reported: $1.2M used in operations in 1997, $6.5M held at year-end, no bank indebtedness
unknowns: how much was sought, how much the negotiation moved, who set the price, whether a higher price was attempted

rationale: no rationale for the price is printed anywhere in the corpus
